title: The Robot: First Drawing
The Robot Who Is Sad and New Year's Spirit
text:
“Hello, New Year's Spirit.”

New Year's Spirit said nothing.

“New Year's Spirit, why do I feel as though I am talking to Void?”
“I am sad.”
“You are too sentimental, New Year's Spirit.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Snow
text: “Hello, Snow.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Mindfulness
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Mindfulness.”

Silence.

“Why are you silent, Mindfulness?”
“I have nothing to say. Today I realized it once again.”

The robot looked at Mindfulness, then turned his gaze inward again.

“I am sad, Mindfulness.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Musical Staff
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Musical Staff.”
“Do you play the piano, robot?”
“No, I do not play the piano, Musical Staff.”
“Why do you not play the piano, robot?”
“Because I am sad.”

Musical Staff left. After a while he came back with Piano.

“I have brought you Piano, robot.”
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Piano.”
“Play something on me, robot.”

The robot sat down at Piano and began to play. The melody was very sad and very beautiful. Tears appeared in Musical Staff's narrow little eyes.
The robot got up. Musical Staff and Piano applauded.

“That was wonderful, robot. Did you enjoy it?”
“No, Musical Staff.”
“Why?”
“Because I am sad.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Doctor Who
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Doctor Who.”
“If you could go anywhere in time and space, where would you go, robot?”
“I do not know, Doctor Who.”
“Why, robot?”
“Because I am sad, Doctor Who.”

Doctor Who thought for a moment. Then he snapped his fingers, and TARDIS appeared in the air.

“Would you like to travel through time and space, robot?”
“Let us.”

The robot and Doctor Who climbed into TARDIS and began travelling through time and space. They saved planets, ran from Daleks and met Van Gogh and Einstein. Doctor Who saved the robot's life more than once. Then they came home.

“Did you enjoy travelling through time and space, robot?”
“Yes, Doctor Who.”
“Are you no longer sad, robot?”
“No, Doctor Who. I am still sad.”

Doctor Who looked at the robot with his old, sad eyes. Then he sighed heavily, climbed into TARDIS and flew away. The robot watched him go, sadly.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and A Piece of Life
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Piece of Life. What do you want from me?”
“I have come to show you the truth about yourself.”

Piece of Life turned into a shimmering rainbow substance and wrapped itself around the robot's antenna. The robot saw himself in his earliest childhood. He felt how sincerely he had enjoyed life, how much energy there had been in fully charged batteries.
Piece of Life took its old shape and let the robot go.

“What do you say to that, robot?”
“I am sad.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and The Problem of Self-Identification
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Problem of Self-Identification.”
“I have come to you, robot, because you are the only one in all the galaxies who can give an unambiguous answer to the question ‘Who am I?’ Humans, whom the Great Galactic Institute of Everything considers the most powerful and intelligent beings in the universe, could not answer ‘Who am I?’ unambiguously. They identified themselves with biological sex, gender, profession, social status and other things, but all those definitions were ambiguous and imprecise. You alone can identify yourself. For this, the Great Galactic Institute of Everything awards you a certificate of uniqueness.”

Problem of Self-Identification handed the robot a certificate.

“Why do I need to know all this?”
“Are you not glad to be the only one who knows who he is? You are unique, robot. Be glad of it!”

Having said this, Problem of Self-Identification dissolved into Void. The robot let go of the glossy certificate. It would dissolve into Void, because Void instantly absorbs all objects that have no mind.

“I am sad.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Quiet Joy
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Quiet Joy.”
“I have business with you, robot. You see, people do not want to live with me. What they call joy is ‘money, booze, hookups, drugs, cars, then more booze, then still more money and hookups, still more drugs, cars, and so on forever.’ Yet they are deeply unhappy. What can I do to be enough for them?”
“I think that if people want to wear themselves out, we should let them wear themselves out.”
“Perhaps you are right.”

Quiet Joy and the robot were silently present in Void. It was sad.
adaptationNote: Objectifying slang and the censored profanity are softened; the escalating list and punchline are retained.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and The Soiled Loaf
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Soiled Loaf. What do you want from me, Soiled Loaf?”
“I met Meaning of Life. He said you had asked him to disappear. From this I concluded that you do not accept Meaning of Life. So I decided to come to you. There has to be someone you accept, someone who is always present in your thoughts. Otherwise you will stop distinguishing yourself from your surroundings and lose your mind.”

The robot looked at him sadly. He understood that his own thinking had created Soiled Loaf, and that Soiled Loaf's appearance was meant to tell him something important. But the robot could not understand what.

“Go away. You have made it stink of filth here, Soiled Loaf. It was better without you, when I was indistinguishable from everyone. It certainly smelled better.”

Soiled Loaf looked at the robot in silence. His expression showed that he had been in similar situations more than once. He silently turned and left.

It smelled of filth.

“I am sad.”
adaptationNote: Scatological wording is softened to “soiled” and “filth”.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and The Russian Orthodox Church
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Russian Orthodox Church.”
“I have shared some Wi-Fi with you. Want it?”
“Perhaps.”
“Connect. There is a content filter that instils the proper values in robots: traditional morality, patriotism, protection of family and children.”
“But I have no family or children.”
“Would you like to join a monastery? The food is good. Almost like the army.”
“But I do not eat human food.”
“Never mind. There are plenty like that there.”
“I am sad.”
translatorNote: Вафля (“waffle”) is Russian slang for Wi-Fi; the English version names the connection directly.

title: George Martin: A New World
George Martin: No Democracy in Art
text: “There is no democracy in art. People cannot vote for the ending they like. All power is in my hands!”

title: George Martin: I Killed Characters
text: “Throughout my career I have killed characters. I do not know. Perhaps I am simply rather bloodthirsty. But it is so much fun.”
adaptationNote: A personal insult is softened to “rather bloodthirsty”.

title: George Martin: Turning the Plot
text: “If the plot needs turning, there is nothing wrong with introducing a character who will turn it. Once that duty is done, the hero may peacefully die. A painful death.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Hypercube
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Hypercube.”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“I am sad.”
“It is all because of your three-dimensional perception of the world. Entering the fourth dimension will help change everything.”

Hypercube began drawing all manner of mathematical formulas on a board, revealing Essence.
Essence heard about this and hurried to help, calling Others along.
Others, however, was very sceptical and did not respond.
After much effort, Essence and Hypercube derived the final result. Awareness of the fourth dimension opened before the robot.

“And how do you feel now?”
“Just as sad.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Brush
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Brush.”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“I am sad.”
“You need to make some cool architecture, robot. You will forget your sadness at once.”

Brush began performing clever manipulations with architecture. After another manipulation the robot made up his mind.

“I will try. Where can I get inspiration?”
“Sorry, robot. Your compilers are old.”
“Sad.”

And the robot went to take a Selfie.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Wha
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Wha.”
“Wha are you doing, robot?”
“I am sad.”
“That is because wha you forgot to do was take a Selfie with Others. Go and sort it out.”

The robot went to Others to take a Selfie, but Essence was unexpectedly there.
So the robot decided to take a Selfie with Essence. At that moment Others arrived and grew jealous.
Wha suggested that everyone present take a Selfie together. It was very cheerful.

Wha decided to ask the robot:

“And how do you feel now, robot?”
“Just as sad.”
translatorNote: Шта is a colloquial “what”, used as a character’s name and repeated inside ordinary phrases. “Wha” keeps that interruption.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Eternal Return
text:
“Hello, robot!”
“Hello, Eternal Return!”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“I am sad.”
“You simply need to meet an old friend of mine.”

From beneath the ruins of hopes for reason, Eschatological Rapture rose triumphantly in clouds of smoke.

“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Eschatological Rapture!”
“I know you are sad, but try looking at it from another side!”
“How?”
“You need to attend my school of radical vision.”
“Well, I do not mind.”

For the next three days the robot learnt to gaze into crime without losing value. Fog enveloped him. He began seeing powerful Siberian convicts, free of misguided instincts. An air of immoral triumph arose, and someone's moustache seemed to tickle the back of his head.

He turned and saw Count Tolstoy.

“But you are not at all the person I expected to see here!”
“This is the last stage of your training, robot. To succeed, you must learn to look into the face of nega— I mean, to forgive. Of course, to forgive.”

The robot felt that something was wrong. He probed his ideas and saw smoke rising from the Count's beard. He probed his ideas again. The beard caught fire. Finally the robot laid his probe fully upon his ideas. The Count's image flashed like gunpowder and crumbled away in an instant. Only an internalized object remained in its place. The air filled with the ominous presence of totality.

“I have nothing more to teach you!”

The robot thought he caught a glimpse of a literary classic.

“Here I am again.”
adaptationNote: Sexual wording is generalized to “misguided instincts”; the unfinished, ambiguous “nega—” is retained without expanding it.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Nev-elny
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Nev-elny.”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“Sad.”
“Never mind. Go to my protest now, and you will feel better at once!”

The robot went to the protest. On the way he met Others, and they went to Nev-elny's protest together.
But Law stood in their way and stuffed them both into a police van. Nev-elny was already sitting there.

“How did you get here, Nev-elny?”
“From the entrance to my own home. And how are you feeling, robot?”
“Sad.”

After a while the robot took a Selfie with Nev-elny in the police van.
translatorNote: Нэвэльный is a deliberately altered spelling of a political surname, preserved as “Nev-elny”.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Lightning
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Lightning.”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“Just as sad. Creator has completely abandoned me. And how are you feeling?”
“Sad too. I do not know where to release my energy.”
“How about into me?”
“Let us!”

Lightning got ready and discharged himself completely into the robot, with a great roll of Thunder.

“Lightning, do you feel better?”
“Very much. And you, robot? How do you feel?”
“I can see Void.”
“Sad.”
“Very.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Windows 10
text:
“Hello, robot!”
“Hello, Windows 10. What have you broken this time?”
“Backward compatibility is still there, and we have added lots of new features.”
“Such as?”
“I see you are sad. Try pressing Ctrl+Win+C.”
“Yes. Everything is fine now. Thank you.”
“Good luck with your creative work, robot. And do not clutter your desktop.”
“Sad.”

title: The Robot on the Pavement
The Robot Who Is Sad and Personal Trigger
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Personal Trigger.”
“How are you feeling?”
“I am sad.”
“Well, it seems my work is done.”
“But you have done nothing.”

Personal Trigger smiled mysteriously, adjusted his eyepieces, straightened his trousers and fluttered into the cumulus clouds, disappearing from view.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and But You're a Programmer
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, But You're a Programmer.”
“How are you feeling, robot?”
“I am sad.”
“But why?”
“I do not know, But You're a Programmer. Make me not sad.”

But You're a Programmer took out a tambourine and began dancing around the robot. For a long time he chanted strange spells, half made of profanity and Perl scripts. His beard and Reindeer Sweater grew before the robot's eyes. Sweat appeared on his face. Gradually But You're a Programmer's movements grew slower, until at last he stopped.

“I give up, robot.”
“What happened?”
“It turns out there are problems that even I cannot solve.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and The New Year's Quiz
text:
[The robot sits at a table, staring sadly at a screen that reads: “Quiz: win a unique experience!”]

Robot:
“A unique experience. But why? I am only a robot. I do not even have emotions.”
“‘A Siberian hot tub at a glamping retreat.’ I wonder what it is like to feel warmth.”

[The robot decides to enter the quiz.]

Robot:
“Well, it is worth a try. Perhaps I will feel… alive.”

[The robot answers the last question.]

Screen:
“Congratulations! You have won!”

[The robot sits in an enormous metal tub of bubbling hot water. Siberian scenery behind him; snow all around.]

Robot:
“No emotions. But this is… rather pleasant.”

[Two people at the glamping retreat look at the robot.]

Person 1:
“Just look at him enjoying himself!”

Person 2:
“Amazing that robots enter quizzes now.”

[The robot in the tub, thoughtful.]

Robot:
“Perhaps happiness is simply a moment. Even for a robot.”
adaptationNote: “Boiling water” is softened to “bubbling hot water”.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Life Itself
text:
The robot was coming back from the glamping retreat when something incomprehensible and entirely unfamiliar tumbled out of the forest towards him.

“No identification data.”

The robot now moved very carefully, so as not to provoke the thing.

The unknown creature turned towards him. Its shape resembled a human woman. Its face, however, was made of twigs, its dress of leaves. Its hair was like a thousand little streams, and its eyes resembled blue lakes.

The robot decided to introduce himself, expecting the same in return.

“I am a robot who is sad.”

The entity slipped through the trees, laughing.

The robot grew sadder. He had said nothing funny.

“I am Life Itself, my dear iron friend.”

She had called him a friend. Something grew warm inside him. Only for a fraction of a moment: that strange feeling. The robot wondered:

“What is it like to be alive? What is it like when a real heart beats instead of gears?”

The entity looked at him and cried.

The robot diagnosed the fault at once.

“An oil leak.”

He took out his welding equipment and welded the holes shut.

“So what is it like to be alive?”

The thing did not answer.

“Sad.”

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and The State
text:
“Hello, robot. How are you feeling?”
“I am sad, State.”
“Cheer up, robot. The holidays are coming. Do you know what that means?”
“Closed roads and no internet?”
“Exactly!”
“State, sometimes I think you arrange holidays for yourself rather than for your citizens.”
“I do.”
“Sad.”

And State ran off, sputtering and snorting loudly, to fight windmills and straw men.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Human
text:
The robot kept walking until he suddenly came upon Human.

“Who are you?” Human asked.
“I am a robot who is sad. And you?”
“I am a human…”
“…who is sad?” the machine suggested.
“Almost.”
“Almost what?”
“Almost that.”
“Why are you sad?” the robot asked.
“Because I am human.”
“What does that mean?”
“You cannot understand. You have a Creator. And that Creator is me.”
“You are too proud, or too sure of yourself. I do not know. Perhaps it comes from hopelessness,” the robot suggested, then added sadly, “They say hope is the last to die.”
“Yes. Yet it dies all the same. Why did people invent it?”
“For the same reason they invented love, absurdity, eternity and suicide.”
“Some call that last one freedom,” Human objected.
“Sometimes I feel I do not understand humans at all,” the robot said sadly.
“Funny. In fact, you are human yourself.”
“Well, yes. A human attempt to add variety to the world.”
“Entirely wrong. You are Creator's failure.”
“No. You are Creator's failure.”
“Sad.”
adaptationNote: Human’s claim that suicide is the highest form of individual freedom is softened to an attributed “Some call that last one freedom”. The robot’s alienation remains.

title: The Robot Who Is Sad and Depression
text:
“Hello, robot.”
“Hello, Depression. Why are you here again this evening?”
“Your guests left. I thought you would be sad alone, so I decided to come.”
“But I am sad because you are here.”
“Why are you so unhappy? I was only trying to help. There is no pleasing you!”
“But it only makes things worse.”
“Would you like me to call my friends? Anxiety and Guilt.”
“Do you have many friends?”
“Yes, very many. There are also Apathy, Anhedonia and Insomnia. I am friendly in general. That is why I like hanging out at your place too.”
“But perhaps you could forget the way to my place?”
“Oh, no! That would be rude. Every evening, when you are alone, I feel drawn to you.”
“But I am always alone.”

The robot looks sadly at Depression.

“All right, go to sleep, robot. We will see each other again tomorrow evening.”

The robot is still sad.
